title: The Swamp Where Measurement Becomes Breathing

features.name: drowned survey marker
features.desc-on-touch: A wooden post, tilted, covered in algae and water-line marks. The numbers carved into it have become abstract. You realize you've been reading them as multiple numbers, not one.

features.name: tide-breath keeper
features.desc-on-touch: A rusted station of some kind—a shed or a shelter. Inside, a mechanism that may once have measured water. Now it seems to measure the air's movement in and out. Breathing.

features.name: silted ledger
features.desc-on-touch: Pages so waterlogged they've become translucent. The measurements underneath are still legible, but barely. You wonder if the water is still counting, still breathing.

features.name: measure-mark
features.desc-on-touch: A single incised line in the earth, so faint you almost miss it. It might be a human survey or the edge of the water's own measurement. It breathes with the tide.

features.name: water-pool
features.desc-on-touch: Pooled water, still and deep, reflecting nothing. When you breathe near it, ripples answer. It's keeping count of something very slow.

inscription: here the cartography forgets which direction the breath is moving

file.name: DistrictWaterAuthority_TidalEstimate_1987.txt
file.note: A government measurement log, annotations suggesting someone gave up mid-survey. Margin notes read like meditation: 'tide breathes,' 'measure fails,' 'mark dissolves.' Increasingly personal.

exits.label: back upstream toward the delta's forgetting
into deeper marshes where names dissolve in water
toward cleaner ground where measurement might resume
outward to the open shelf where memory becomes tide
